insight: das Gehirn vs. das Hirn — both mean brain, but Gehirn is the standard medical/formal term; Hirn is informal and also used figuratively: Streng dein Hirn an! (Use your brain!). ⚠ die Leber (liver) vs. liefern (to deliver) — no relation, but beginners often confuse them phonetically. atmen is a regular verb but watch the present tense: ich atme, du atmest (the -e- is inserted for pronunciation). der Atem (breath) is the noun; atmen is the verb — like Schritt (step) and schreiten (to stride).

words.breakdown_note: das Gehirn is the standard term; das Hirn is informal and also used figuratively (Streng dein Hirn an! = Use your brain!).

examples.de: Das menschliche Gehirn ist ein faszinierendes Organ.
examples.en: The human brain is a fascinating organ.

examples.de: Eine Gehirnerschütterung ist eine ernste Verletzung.
examples.en: A concussion is a serious injury.

words.mnemonic: GEHIRN: ge + Hirn — collective brain. Think 'gear-n' — the brain is your mental gear.

words.breakdown_note: das Herz is used both medically (das Herzschlag = heartbeat) and emotionally (von Herzen = from the heart; Herzschmerz = heartache).

examples.de: Das Herz schlägt etwa 70 Mal pro Minute.
examples.en: The heart beats about 70 times per minute.
That touches my heart.

words.mnemonic: HERZ: close to English 'heart' — both from Proto-Germanic *hertô.

breakdown.note: from Old High German lunga = the light organ

words.breakdown_note: Often used in plural: die Lungen. Etymologically related to 'light' — the lung was the 'light (not heavy) organ'. Same root as English 'lung'.

examples.en: Smoking damages the lungs.
He has pneumonia.

words.mnemonic: LUNGE: cognate with English 'lung' — and etymologically 'the light organ'.

breakdown.note: from Old High German lebara — related to leben (to live)

words.breakdown_note: Etymologically linked to leben (to live) — the liver was seen as the seat of life. NOT related to liefern (to deliver), which beginners sometimes confuse phonetically.

examples.de: Die Leber ist das größte innere Organ.
examples.en: The liver is the largest internal organ.
He suffers from a liver disease.

word_family.meaning: to deliver — ⚠ sounds similar, completely unrelated

words.mnemonic: LEBER: LEBER-n = to LIVE. The liver keeps you alive.

words.breakdown_note: Note the conjugation: ich atme, du atmest (the -e- is inserted before -st for pronunciation). Tief atmen = to breathe deeply.

examples.de: Atmen Sie tief ein und wieder aus.
examples.en: Breathe in deeply and out again.

examples.de: In der Höhe ist es schwerer zu atmen.
examples.en: At altitude it is harder to breathe.

words.mnemonic: ATMEN: 'ahtmen' — sounds like the sound of breathing.

examples.de: Ihm blieb der Atem weg vor Staunen.
examples.en: He was breathless with amazement.

examples.de: Sie holte tief Atem vor dem Sprung.
examples.en: She took a deep breath before the jump.

words.mnemonic: ATEM: Sanskrit ātman = breath/soul — ancient, cosmic.

breakdown.note: from Latin musculus = little mouse (muscle moving under skin looks like a mouse)

examples.de: Nach dem Training tun mir alle Muskeln weh.
examples.en: After training all my muscles ache.

examples.de: Er trainiert seine Muskeln im Fitnessstudio.
examples.en: He trains his muscles in the gym.

words.mnemonic: MUSKEL: from Latin musculus = 'little mouse' — a flexed muscle looks like a mouse running under the skin.

insight: krank is the core adjective; die Krankheit is its noun. The verb erkranken (to fall ill) is formal: Er ist an Grippe erkrankt (He came down with flu). ⚠ das Symptom (pl. die Symptome) — borrowed from Greek; always neuter in German. das Fieber specifically means a raised temperature — not just 'fever' in the metaphorical English sense. Fieber messen = to take someone's temperature; Fieber haben = to have a temperature.

breakdown.note: from Old High German kranc = weak, feeble

examples.de: Sie war eine Woche lang krank.
examples.en: She was ill for a week.
He called in sick.

words.grammar_notes: krank sein = to be ill. erkranken = to fall ill (formal, + an + Dative: an Grippe erkranken). krank machen = to make sick; sich krank melden = to call in sick.
words.mnemonic: KRANK: sounds like 'crank' — feeling cranky because you're sick.

examples.en: The illness lasted three weeks.
Many diseases are curable.

words.mnemonic: KRANK-HEIT: krank + -heit = 'the state of being sick'.

words.breakdown_note: Plural: die Symptome. Always neuter in German. A loanword from Greek via Latin.

examples.en: What symptoms do you have?

examples.de: Fieber ist ein typisches Symptom einer Erkältung.
examples.en: Fever is a typical symptom of a cold.

words.mnemonic: SYMPTOM: identical to English — Greek loanword in both languages.

words.breakdown_note: Fieber specifically means a raised body temperature. Fieber haben = to have a fever; Fieber messen = to take a temperature. Not used metaphorically as freely as English 'fever'.

examples.en: The child has a high fever.

examples.de: Das Fieber ist über Nacht gesunken.
examples.en: The fever went down overnight.

word_family.meaning: to have a fever; to be feverishly excited

words.mnemonic: FIEBER: from Latin febris — the FEVER burns.

examples.en: He has a bad cough.
The cough won't stop.

words.mnemonic: HUSTEN: sounds like 'hoost-en' — the WHOOSHING sound of coughing.

examples.en: He coughed all night.

examples.de: Bitte husten Sie in Ihre Armbeuge.
examples.en: Please cough into your elbow.

words.mnemonic: HUSTEN: onomatopoeic — 'hoost!' — that's the sound.

words.breakdown_note: Literally 'the cooling' — catching a cold was seen as the result of getting chilled. Eine Erkältung bekommen / haben = to catch / have a cold.

examples.en: I have a bad cold.

examples.de: Bei einer Erkältung hilft viel Ruhe.
examples.en: For a cold, lots of rest helps.

word_family.meaning: influenza/flu — ⚠ much more serious than Erkältung

words.mnemonic: ERKÄLTUNG: er-KÄLT-ung — the body getting COLD (kalt) and catching it.

insight: das Rezept has two completely different everyday meanings: (1) a doctor's prescription and (2) a cooking recipe. Context always makes it clear — auf Rezept (on prescription) vs. das Rezept für Kuchen (cake recipe). ⚠ die Praxis (doctor's surgery/practice) vs. die Praxis (practice/application in abstract sense) — same word, two meanings: in der Praxis (in practice) vs. in die Praxis gehen (go to the doctor). der Befund = medical finding/result — from befinden (to find/assess), not to be confused with der Fund (a find/discovery).

examples.de: Der Arzt untersuchte den Patienten gründlich.
examples.en: The doctor examined the patient thoroughly.
The police investigated the crime scene.

words.mnemonic: UNTERSUCHEN: thorough-SUCHEN (searching) — examining thoroughly.

examples.en: The examination found nothing.
He needs a thorough examination.

words.mnemonic: UNTERSUCHUNG: the -ung nominalises untersuchen — 'the examination'.

words.breakdown_note: Also means 'to write incorrectly' (sich verschreiben = to make a writing error). Context makes the meaning clear.

examples.en: The doctor prescribed her antibiotics.
The medication requires a prescription.

word_family.meaning: to make a writing error — ⚠ same verb, different meaning

words.mnemonic: VER-SCHREIB-en: WRITE (schreiben) a prescription — ver- makes it 'for/towards'.

words.breakdown_note: das Rezept has two everyday meanings: (1) a doctor's prescription (auf Rezept = on prescription) and (2) a cooking recipe. Context always clarifies.

examples.de: Der Arzt hat mir ein Rezept ausgestellt.
examples.en: The doctor issued me a prescription.

examples.de: Das Rezept für diesen Kuchen ist geheim.
examples.en: The recipe for this cake is secret.

word_family.meaning: cooking recipe — ⚠ same word, different domain

words.mnemonic: REZEPT: 'reh-TSEPT' — a recipe for medicine OR food. Latin receptum.

examples.en: The diagnosis was diabetes.

examples.de: Eine frühe Diagnose verbessert die Heilungschancen.
examples.en: An early diagnosis improves the chances of recovery.

word_family.meaning: medical finding — what leads to the diagnosis

words.mnemonic: DIAGNOSE: dia (through) + gnose (knowledge) — knowing through examination. Same as English.

words.breakdown_note: Two meanings: (1) a doctor's or dentist's office/surgery (in die Praxis gehen) and (2) practical application as opposed to theory (in der Praxis = in practice).

examples.en: The surgery/practice is closed on Mondays.

examples.de: In der Praxis sieht das anders aus.
examples.en: In practice it looks different.

words.mnemonic: PRAXIS: Greek for 'doing' — both the doctor's doing-place AND the act of doing.

words.breakdown_note: der Befund = what the doctor/test finds. Der Befund ist unauffällig = the results are unremarkable (normal). Do not confuse with der Fund (a discovery/find in general contexts).

examples.en: The result was positive, unfortunately.
All findings/results are normal.

word_family.meaning: to find; sich befinden = to be located

words.mnemonic: BE-FUND: what is beFUNDen (found) by the doctor — the finding.

insight: einnehmen (separable) = to take medication: Nehmen Sie die Tablette zweimal täglich ein. ⚠ die Nebenwirkung (side effect) = Neben (beside/secondary) + Wirkung (effect) — a beautifully transparent compound. Contrast: die Wirkung (the intended effect). verträglich = tolerable/compatible (gut verträglich = well-tolerated); unverträglich = intolerable — both come from tragen (to bear/carry): verträglich literally means 'bearable'. Also: Nahrungsmittelunverträglichkeit = food intolerance.

words.breakdown_note: Plural: die Medikamente. More formal than das Mittel (remedy). Also: die Arznei (archaic/formal). Ein Medikament einnehmen = to take a medication.

examples.de: Das Medikament muss zweimal täglich eingenommen werden.
examples.en: The medication must be taken twice daily.
Prescription medications require a prescription.

words.mnemonic: MEDIKAMENT: medi-KAMENT — 'medi' = medicine, from Latin medicus (doctor).

breakdown.note: from French tablette = small tablet, from Latin tabula = board

examples.de: Nehmen Sie bitte zwei Tabletten nach dem Essen.
examples.en: Please take two tablets after meals.

examples.de: Die Tabletten müssen mit viel Wasser eingenommen werden.
examples.en: The tablets must be taken with plenty of water.

words.mnemonic: TABLETTE: like a little TABLE (tabula) — a flat pill.

breakdown.note: from Greek dosis = a giving, from didōmi = to give

words.breakdown_note: Plural: die Dosen OR die Dosierungen. Die richtige Dosis = the correct dose. Überdosierung = overdose.

examples.de: Die Dosis muss vom Arzt festgelegt werden.
examples.en: The dose must be determined by the doctor.

examples.de: Eine zu hohe Dosis ist gefährlich.
examples.en: Too high a dose is dangerous.

words.mnemonic: DOSIS: Greek 'dosis' = a giving — what is given to you by the doctor. Same in English.

words.breakdown_note: Literally 'secondary effect' — Wirkung = intended effect; Nebenwirkung = unintended side effect. A beautifully transparent compound.

examples.en: The medication has strong side effects.

examples.de: Lesen Sie die Liste der Nebenwirkungen sorgfältig.
examples.en: Read the list of side effects carefully.

words.mnemonic: NEBEN-WIRKUNG: the EFFECT (Wirkung) that happens BESIDE (neben) the main one.

words.english: to take (medication); to occupy; to earn
words.breakdown_note: Multiple meanings: (1) to take medication (zweimal täglich einnehmen), (2) to occupy a position/place (eine wichtige Stelle einnehmen), (3) to earn/take in money.

examples.de: Nehmen Sie die Tablette nach dem Frühstück ein.
examples.en: Take the tablet after breakfast.

examples.de: Er nimmt eine wichtige Position im Unternehmen ein.
examples.en: He occupies an important position in the company.

words.mnemonic: EIN-NEHMEN: take IN (ein) — swallow it in.

words.breakdown_note: From tragen (to bear/carry) → verträglich = bearable, tolerable. Gut verträglich = well-tolerated (medication). Also used for people: ein verträglicher Mensch = an easy-going person.

examples.en: The medication is well-tolerated.

examples.de: Er ist ein sehr verträglicher Mensch.
examples.en: He is a very easy-going person.

words.mnemonic: VERTRÄGLICH: VER-TRAG-lich — like a TREATY (Vertrag) — it agrees with you.

examples.en: Some people are lactose intolerant.

examples.de: Dieses Medikament ist mit Alkohol unverträglich.
examples.en: This medication is incompatible with alcohol.

words.mnemonic: UN-VERTRÄGLICH: the un- prefix flips verträglich — incompatible, intolerable.

insight: heilen (to heal/cure) vs. heilig (holy/sacred) — same root heilen (whole, healthy): health, healing, and holiness all come from the same Proto-Germanic concept of wholeness. ⚠ sich erholen (to recover/recuperate) vs. holen (to fetch/get) — er-holen literally means 'to fetch oneself back' to full capacity. genesen is a formal/literary verb for recovery: Er ist genesen (He has recovered). Prefer sich erholen in everyday speech; genesen appears in medical reports and literature.

words.english: to treat (medically); to handle, to deal with

examples.de: Der Arzt behandelt sie mit Antibiotika.
examples.en: The doctor is treating her with antibiotics.
How do you handle this problem?

words.grammar_notes: Two main meanings: (1) medical treatment (Der Arzt behandelt den Patienten) and (2) to deal with/handle something (ein Thema behandeln = to cover a topic).
words.mnemonic: BE-HANDELN: to put your HANDS (Hand) to something — to handle/treat.

examples.en: The treatment lasts six weeks.
He is under medical treatment.

words.mnemonic: BEHANDLUNG: behandeln + -ung = 'the treatment'.

words.breakdown_note: heilen can be transitive (to cure someone: Der Arzt heilte ihn) or intransitive (to heal: Die Wunde heilt). Root heil- = whole, healthy — connected to 'holy' and 'health' historically.

conjugation.note: weak; uses sein when intransitive (wound heals itself)

examples.en: The wound has healed well.
This disease is not curable.

word_family.meaning: holy, sacred — ⚠ same root heil-, different meaning

words.mnemonic: HEILEN: heil = whole — to make whole again. Healing = restoring wholeness.

examples.en: The healing/recovery took several months.

examples.de: Es gibt keine Heilung für diese Krankheit.
examples.en: There is no cure for this disease.

words.mnemonic: HEILUNG: heilen + -ung = 'the act of healing'. -ung nominalises the verb.

examples.de: Sie erholt sich gut von der Operation.
examples.en: She is recovering well from the operation.

examples.de: Er braucht Zeit, um sich zu erholen.
examples.en: He needs time to recuperate.

words.grammar_notes: sich erholen von + Dative = to recover from: Ich erhole mich von der Operation.

word_family.meaning: to fetch — ⚠ the base verb, different meaning

words.mnemonic: SICH ERHOLEN: fetch (holen) yourself back to health — er-holen.

examples.en: He urgently needs rest and recovery.
The holiday serves for recuperation.

words.mnemonic: ERHOLUNG: -ung nominalises sich erholen — 'the state of recovery'.

breakdown.note: Old High German: nesen = to be saved, to survive

words.breakdown_note: Formal and literary synonym for sich erholen. Er ist genesen appears in medical reports; prefer sich erholen in everyday speech.

examples.de: Er ist vollständig von seiner Krankheit genesen.
examples.en: He has fully recovered from his illness.
Those convalescing need a lot of rest.

words.mnemonic: GENESEN: sounds like 'ge-NAZE-en' — to be SAVED from illness. Ancient, formal.

insight: vorbeugen (separable) = to prevent: vor (before) + beugen (to bend) — literally 'to bend forward before something happens'; the sense evolved to mean preventing illness. ⚠ die Vorsorge (prevention/precaution) vs. die Fürsorge (care/welfare) — both have Sorge (care/worry) at their core: vor- (before) vs. für- (for). die Impfung (vaccination) comes from impfen, which originally meant to graft a plant — the same 'insertion' metaphor as the English 'inoculate'.

words.english: to prevent, to take precautions against
words.breakdown_note: Literally 'to bend forward before something happens'. Takes Dative: einer Krankheit vorbeugen = to prevent a disease.

examples.de: Regelmäßige Bewegung beugt vielen Krankheiten vor.
examples.en: Regular exercise prevents many diseases.
Vaccinations prevent infections.

words.mnemonic: VOR-BEUGEN: BEND (beugen) FORWARD (vor) — lean in before it happens.

words.breakdown_note: Literally 'caring before' something goes wrong. die Vorsorgeuntersuchung = preventive health check-up (very common in German healthcare).

examples.de: Zur Vorsorge sollte man regelmäßig zum Arzt gehen.
examples.en: As a precaution one should go to the doctor regularly.
The preventive check-up is free.

word_family.meaning: welfare, care — ⚠ für = for (people in need), not vor (before)

words.mnemonic: VOR-SORGE: CARE (Sorge) BEFORE (vor) — caring in advance.

words.breakdown_note: impfen originally meant to graft a plant (inserting a cutting into rootstock) — the same insertion metaphor as inoculation. Sich impfen lassen = to get vaccinated.

examples.en: The flu vaccination is recommended annually.
Do you have all your vaccinations?

words.mnemonic: IMPFUNG: from 'impfen' — the GRAFT that protects. Same idea as 'inoculate'.

words.breakdown_note: lassen + infinitive = to have something done (causative). sich impfen lassen = to have yourself vaccinated (by someone else). Very common construction in German.

examples.de: Ich habe mich gegen Tetanus impfen lassen.
examples.en: I got vaccinated against tetanus.

examples.de: Lassen Sie sich so früh wie möglich impfen.
examples.en: Get vaccinated as early as possible.

words.mnemonic: SICH IMPFEN LASSEN: let yourself be vaccinated — lassen = have it done.

examples.de: Sonnencreme schützt die Haut vor UV-Strahlen.
examples.en: Sunscreen protects the skin from UV rays.
We must protect the environment.

words.grammar_notes: schützen vor + Dative = to protect from: Die Impfung schützt vor der Grippe.
words.mnemonic: SCHÜTZEN: SCHÜTZ = shield — to shield/protect.

examples.de: Der Helm bietet Schutz vor Verletzungen.
examples.en: The helmet provides protection against injuries.

examples.de: Unter dem Schutz des Gesetzes stehen.
examples.en: To be under the protection of the law.

words.mnemonic: SCHUTZ: the SHOOT (Schuss?) — no, think SHIELD. Protection.

examples.en: Skydiving is a high-risk sport.
That is a risky undertaking.

words.mnemonic: RISIKO-REICH: RICH in RISK — full of danger.

insight: Sport treiben is the standard German phrase for doing sports — never *Sport machen (that's an anglicism). Ich treibe Sport = I do sport/exercise. ⚠ die Ausdauer (stamina/endurance/perseverance) = aus (through to the end) + dauern (to last) — the same word used for physical endurance AND mental perseverance: Er hat viel Ausdauer (He has a lot of stamina / He is very persistent). ausgewogen (balanced) = aus (out) + gewogen (weighed) — literally 'weighed out evenly'.

words.english: to eat, to feed oneself, to live on (a diet)

examples.en: She follows a vegetarian diet.
He alone supports/feeds his family.

words.grammar_notes: sich ernähren von + Dative = to live on, to eat: Er ernährt sich von Obst und Gemüse.
words.mnemonic: SICH ERNÄHREN: er-NÄHR-en — nourishing (Nahrung) yourself.

examples.en: A healthy diet is important.
Diet influences health.

words.mnemonic: ERNÄHRUNG: ernähren + -ung = 'the diet/nutrition'.

words.breakdown_note: Literally 'weighed out evenly' — balanced in all respects. Eine ausgewogene Ernährung = a balanced diet.

examples.de: Eine ausgewogene Ernährung enthält alle Nährstoffe.
examples.en: A balanced diet contains all nutrients.
The verdict was balanced/fair.

words.mnemonic: AUS-GE-WOGEN: weighed OUT — perfectly balanced on the scales.

words.breakdown_note: Literally 'nourishing substance'. Plural: die Nährstoffe. Nährstoffreich = nutrient-rich; nährstoffarm = nutrient-poor.

examples.de: Obst und Gemüse sind reich an Nährstoffen.
examples.en: Fruit and vegetables are rich in nutrients.
The body needs various nutrients.

words.mnemonic: NÄHR-STOFF: nourishing (nähr-) SUBSTANCE (Stoff) — nutrient.

words.breakdown_note: The standard German phrase for doing sport. Never *Sport machen — that is an anglicism. Treiben here means to pursue/engage in an activity.

examples.de: Sie treibt dreimal pro Woche Sport.
examples.en: She does sport three times a week.

examples.de: Regelmäßig Sport zu treiben ist gesund.
examples.en: Doing sport regularly is healthy.

words.mnemonic: SPORT TREIBEN: you DRIVE yourself to do sport. Treiben = pursue.

examples.en: He trains daily at the gym.

examples.de: Die Mannschaft trainiert für das nächste Spiel.
examples.en: The team is training for the next game.

words.mnemonic: TRAINIEREN: from French entraîner — same as English 'to train'.

words.breakdown_note: Used for both physical endurance (sport) AND mental perseverance. Er hat viel Ausdauer = He has great stamina / He is very persistent.

examples.en: Endurance training strengthens the heart.
This task requires a lot of perseverance.

words.mnemonic: AUS-DAUER: lasting (dauern) all the way OUT (aus) — endurance.

insight: sich verletzen is reflexive: Ich habe mich verletzt (I hurt myself). For a specific body part, add the Accusative: Ich habe mir den Arm verletzt (I injured my arm) — note the Dative reflexive mir here, because der Arm is already the Accusative object. ⚠ verbinden (to bandage) vs. sich verbinden (to connect/unite) — same verb, very different contexts. der Verband = dressing/bandage (medical) AND association/federation (organisational) — always check context.

words.english: to injure oneself, to hurt oneself

examples.de: Sie hat sich beim Sport verletzt.
examples.en: She injured herself doing sport.

examples.de: Er hat sich den Knöchel verstaucht.
examples.en: He sprained his ankle.

words.grammar_notes: For a body part: sich + Dative + Accusative: Ich habe mir den Arm verletzt (the arm is the Acc. object; mir = Dat. reflexive).
words.mnemonic: SICH VERLETZEN: ver- intensifies the harm — to seriously hurt yourself.

examples.en: The injury is healing well.
He suffered a serious injury.

words.mnemonic: VERLETZUNG: -ung makes the verb into the noun — 'the injury'.

words.breakdown_note: Literally 'a bad fall/occurrence'. Der Unfall passiert = an accident happens. einen Unfall haben = to have an accident. der Arbeitsunfall = workplace accident.

examples.de: Es gab einen schweren Unfall auf der Autobahn.
examples.en: There was a serious accident on the motorway.
Was there an accident?

word_family.meaning: fall; case — ⚠ Unfall is not just a fall

words.mnemonic: UN-FALL: an UNhappy FALL — an accident.

words.breakdown_note: die Wunde = an open wound or cut. Die Wunde verbinden = to dress/bandage a wound. Die Wunde heilt = the wound heals.

examples.en: The wound must be disinfected.

examples.de: Er hatte eine tiefe Wunde am Arm.
examples.en: He had a deep wound on his arm.

words.mnemonic: WUNDE: 'VOON-duh' — cognate with English 'wound'.

words.english: to bandage; to connect, to link
words.breakdown_note: Two main meanings: (1) medical: to dress/bandage a wound (jemanden verbinden); (2) to connect/link things or people (Städte verbinden = to connect cities).

examples.en: The paramedic bandaged the wound.

examples.de: Eine Brücke verbindet die beiden Stadtteile.
examples.en: A bridge connects the two districts.

words.mnemonic: VER-BIND-EN: BIND together — both wound-binding and connecting.

words.breakdown_note: der Verband has two completely different meanings: (1) a medical bandage/dressing and (2) an association or federation (Sportverband = sports federation). Always check context.

examples.de: Der Verband muss täglich gewechselt werden.
examples.en: The dressing must be changed daily.

examples.de: Er ist Mitglied im Deutschen Fußball-Verband.
examples.en: He is a member of the German Football Association.

word_family.meaning: connection — ⚠ not the same as Verband

words.mnemonic: VERBAND: VER-BAND — it BANDS (binds) the wound. Also bands people together (federation).

examples.en: The wound is bleeding heavily.

examples.de: Er hat geblutet und musste ins Krankenhaus.
examples.en: He bled and had to go to hospital.

words.mnemonic: BLUTEN: Blut (blood) + -en — to BLOOD, i.e. to bleed.

insight: stationär (inpatient) vs. ambulant (outpatient) — the essential hospital pair. ⚠ ambulant looks like 'ambulance' but die Ambulanz is the emergency department / outpatient clinic, not the vehicle — der Krankenwagen or der Rettungswagen is the ambulance vehicle. operieren takes a direct object: Der Arzt operiert den Patienten — but you can also say: Der Patient wird operiert (passive). die Notaufnahme = emergency admissions; der Notfall = the emergency itself.

words.breakdown_note: Literally 'house of the sick'. ins Krankenhaus = to hospital; im Krankenhaus = in hospital. Colloquial synonym: die Klinik.

examples.de: Er muss ins Krankenhaus eingeliefert werden.
examples.en: He has to be admitted to hospital.

examples.de: Sie arbeitet im Krankenhaus als Pflegerin.
examples.en: She works as a nurse in the hospital.

words.mnemonic: KRANKEN-HAUS: the HOUSE (Haus) for SICK PEOPLE (Kranken).

words.breakdown_note: stationär = admitted to a hospital ward (staying overnight/longer). Antonym: ambulant = outpatient. Stationär behandelt werden = to be treated as an inpatient.

examples.en: He is being treated as an inpatient.

examples.de: Nach der Operation blieb sie drei Tage stationär.
examples.en: After the operation she stayed three days as an inpatient.

words.mnemonic: STATIONÄR: staying on the STATION (ward) — inpatient.

words.breakdown_note: ambulant = treated without hospital admission. ⚠ die Ambulanz in German = the emergency/outpatient department of a hospital, NOT the vehicle. Der Krankenwagen / der Rettungswagen = the ambulance vehicle.

examples.de: Die Operation kann ambulant durchgeführt werden.
examples.en: The operation can be done on an outpatient basis.

examples.de: Er wird ambulant in der Klinik behandelt.
examples.en: He is treated as an outpatient at the clinic.

words.mnemonic: AMBULANT: ambulare = to walk — the patient walks in and walks out.

examples.de: Er wurde sofort in die Notaufnahme gebracht.
examples.en: He was taken straight to the emergency room.

examples.de: Die Notaufnahme ist rund um die Uhr geöffnet.
examples.en: The A&E is open 24/7.

word_family.meaning: to admit, to receive, to record

words.mnemonic: NOT-AUFNAHME: ADMISSION (Aufnahme) in DISTRESS (Not) — the A&E.

examples.en: In an emergency please call 112.
This is not an emergency.

word_family.meaning: if necessary, in case of emergency
accident — ⚠ Unfall = accident; Notfall = emergency situation

words.mnemonic: NOT-FALL: a distressing (Not) case (Fall) — an emergency.

examples.en: She was operated on on her heart.
The surgeon operated successfully.

words.grammar_notes: Transitive: Der Arzt operiert den Patienten. Or passive: Der Patient wird operiert. Sich operieren lassen = to have an operation.
words.mnemonic: OPERIEREN: Latin operari = to work. The surgeon OPERATES = works on you.

examples.en: The operation lasted four hours.

examples.de: Nach der Operation braucht man Ruhe.
examples.en: After the operation one needs rest.

word_family.meaning: to operate on an outpatient basis

words.mnemonic: OPERATION: same as English — Latin operatio. Known internationally.

insight: deprimiert is the past participle of deprimieren used as adjective — borrowed from Latin deprimere (to press down). ⚠ die Depression (clinical depression) vs. deprimiert (feeling depressed today) — use deprimiert for a current mood; die Depression for the diagnosed condition. die Stressbewältigung = Stress + Bewältigung (coping/mastering) — Bewältigung comes from walten (to rule/govern): to master/overcome stress. entspannen is separable in some uses: Ich entspanne mich (I relax) — always reflexive for 'I relax'.

breakdown.note: from Latin deprimere = to press down

words.breakdown_note: deprimiert = feeling depressed (current state). die Depression = the clinical condition. Don't use deprimiert for clinical diagnosis.

examples.en: I am very down/depressed today.

examples.de: Das schlechte Wetter macht mich deprimiert.
examples.en: The bad weather makes me feel low.

word_family.meaning: to depress, to get someone down
⚠ clinical condition, not just a bad day

words.mnemonic: DEPRIMIERT: de-PRESS-ed — pressed down.

words.breakdown_note: die Depression refers to the clinical mental health condition. For everyday low mood, use deprimiert or niedergeschlagen. Also used in economics: wirtschaftliche Depression.

examples.de: Sie leidet an einer schweren Depression.
examples.en: She suffers from severe depression.

examples.de: Eine Depression ist eine ernste Erkrankung.
examples.en: Depression is a serious illness.

words.mnemonic: DEPRESSION: same as English — Latin depressio. Pressing down on the spirit.

words.breakdown_note: An English loanword used in German psychology and medicine. Synonym: das Ausgebranntsein. Einen Burn-out erleiden = to suffer burnout.

examples.de: Er hat einen Burn-out erlitten und arbeitet nicht mehr.
examples.en: He suffered a burnout and is no longer working.

examples.de: Burn-out ist im modernen Arbeitsleben häufig.
examples.en: Burnout is common in modern working life.

words.mnemonic: BURN-OUT: English loanword — the fire burned out completely.

words.breakdown_note: bewältigen = to master, to overcome. Stressbewältigung = overcoming/managing stress. Ein wichtiges Thema in der modernen Arbeitswelt.

examples.de: Yoga ist eine wirksame Methode zur Stressbewältigung.
examples.en: Yoga is an effective method of stress management.
Stress management must be practised.

words.mnemonic: STRESS-BEWÄLTIGUNG: MASTERING (Bewältigung) your STRESS.

words.breakdown_note: Literally 'to remove tension'. Can be reflexive (sich entspannen = to relax) or transitive (Musik entspannt mich = music relaxes me).

examples.de: Ich entspanne mich am liebsten beim Lesen.
examples.en: I prefer to relax while reading.
Music relaxes me a great deal.

words.mnemonic: ENT-SPANNEN: remove (ent-) the TENSION (Spannung) — relax.

examples.en: For relaxation I go swimming.
Political relaxation/détente between the countries.

word_family.meaning: tension — ⚠ direct antonym: an- vs. ent-

words.mnemonic: ENTSPANNUNG: relaxation — -ung turns the verb into the noun.

breakdown.note: from Latin meditari = to think over

examples.en: She meditates twenty minutes daily.
Meditating helps with stress.

words.mnemonic: MEDITIEREN: same as 'to meditate' — Latin meditari.

insight: schmerzen is the verb form: Mein Rücken schmerzt (My back hurts/aches) — more formal than wehtun. ⚠ chronisch (chronic) vs. akut (acute) — both from Latin/Greek medical terms: chronisch = long-lasting (from chronos, time); akut = immediate/urgent (from acutus, sharp). die Beschwerde (pl. die Beschwerden) = complaint/ailment — in medical German, Beschwerden are the symptoms a patient reports: Welche Beschwerden haben Sie? (What symptoms do you have?)

words.english: to hurt, to ache, to pain
words.breakdown_note: More formal than wehtun. Mein Rücken schmerzt = My back aches. Also used figuratively: Das schmerzt mich = That pains me (emotionally).

examples.en: My knee hurts when climbing stairs.

examples.de: Es schmerzt mich, so etwas zu hören.
examples.en: It pains me to hear something like that.

words.mnemonic: SCHMERZEN: Schmerz + -en — the pain SMARTS.

examples.en: The injury is very painful.
It is a painful process.

word_family.meaning: painful (emotionally) — ⚠ -lich = emotional pain; -haft = physical pain often

words.mnemonic: SCHMERZ-HAFT: having (-haft) the quality of pain (Schmerz).

words.breakdown_note: Usually used in plural: die Kopfschmerzen (I have a headache = Ich habe Kopfschmerzen). Also: Kopfweh (more colloquial).

examples.en: I have terrible headaches.
Aspirin often helps against headaches.

words.mnemonic: KOPF-SCHMERZ: HEAD (Kopf) + PAIN (Schmerz). Head pain.

words.breakdown_note: Usually plural: Rückenschmerzen haben. Very common complaint: Rückenschmerzen sind eine Volkskrankheit.

examples.en: I have chronic back pain.

examples.de: Rückenschmerzen sind in Deutschland sehr verbreitet.
examples.en: Back pain is very widespread in Germany.

words.mnemonic: RÜCKEN-SCHMERZ: BACK (Rücken) + PAIN (Schmerz).

words.breakdown_note: chronisch = long-lasting, persistent (weeks/months/years). Opposite: akut (acute = sudden onset, short-term). Chronische Schmerzen = chronic pain.

examples.en: He suffers from chronic back pain.
Chronic diseases require long-term treatment.

words.mnemonic: CHRONISCH: CHRON-isch = TIME-ish — it goes on and on over time.

words.breakdown_note: akut = sudden onset, urgent, immediate — the opposite of chronisch. Ein akutes Problem = an urgent/pressing problem. Akute Schmerzen = sudden/sharp pain.

examples.en: The patient had acute abdominal pain.

examples.de: Das ist ein akutes Problem, das sofort gelöst werden muss.
examples.en: That is an urgent problem that must be solved immediately.

words.mnemonic: AKUT: ACUTE — sharp, sudden, RIGHT NOW. Same as English.

words.breakdown_note: Two important uses: (1) a complaint (formal: eine Beschwerde einreichen = to file a complaint) and (2) medical Beschwerden (pl.) = symptoms a patient reports. Welche Beschwerden haben Sie? is what a German doctor asks.

examples.en: What symptoms/complaints do you have?

examples.de: Er reichte eine Beschwerde beim Chef ein.
examples.en: He filed a complaint with the boss.

words.mnemonic: BESCHWERDE: be-SCHWER-de — something HEAVY (schwer) weighing on you.

insight: einschlafen is separable: Ich schlafe ein — and it is also used for a limb falling asleep: Mein Fuß ist eingeschlafen (My foot has gone to sleep). ⚠ die Schlaflosigkeit (insomnia) = Schlaf (sleep) + los (without) + igkeit (noun suffix) — literally 'sleep-lessness'. Compare: arbeitslos (unemployed), hoffnungslos (hopeless). ausgeruht (rested/refreshed) = aus + geruht (past participle of ruhen, to rest) — feeling 'fully rested out'. Contrast: erschöpft (exhausted).

conjugation.note: strong verb; er schläft (vowel change in present)

examples.de: Ich habe heute Nacht schlecht geschlafen.
examples.en: I slept badly last night.

examples.de: Wie viele Stunden schläfst du pro Nacht?
examples.en: How many hours do you sleep per night?

words.mnemonic: SCHLAFEN: strong verb — schlief, geschlafen. Think 'to SLEEP'.

examples.en: Eight hours of sleep are ideal.
I am lacking sleep.

words.mnemonic: SCHLAF: the noun of schlafen. SLEEP.

words.english: to fall asleep; (of a limb) to go to sleep/go numb
words.breakdown_note: Uses sein as auxiliary (change of state). Also used when a limb goes numb: Mein Bein ist eingeschlafen.

conjugation.note: separable strong verb; uses sein (change of state)

examples.en: I fell asleep immediately.
My foot has gone to sleep (gone numb).

word_family.meaning: to sleep in, to have a full sleep

words.mnemonic: EIN-SCHLAFEN: fall IN-to sleep — ist eingeschlafen (sein verb).

conjugation.note: separable weak verb; uses sein (change of state)

examples.de: Ich wache jeden Morgen um sechs Uhr auf.
examples.en: I wake up every morning at six o'clock.

examples.de: Er ist mitten in der Nacht aufgewacht.
examples.en: He woke up in the middle of the night.

words.mnemonic: AUF-WACHEN: wake UP (auf) — ist aufgewacht (sein verb).

words.breakdown_note: Literally 'sleep-less-ness'. Very transparent compound: Schlaf + los + -igkeit. Medical term: die Insomnie (loanword). An schlaflosen Nächten leiden = to suffer from sleepless nights.

examples.en: She suffers from chronic insomnia.

examples.de: Stress ist häufig die Ursache von Schlaflosigkeit.
examples.en: Stress is often the cause of insomnia.

words.mnemonic: SCHLAF-LOS-IGKEIT: sleep (Schlaf) + without (-los) + -igkeit = sleeplessness.

examples.en: He spent a sleepless night.
I lay sleepless in bed.

words.mnemonic: SCHLAF-LOS: without (-los) sleep (Schlaf) — sleepless.

words.breakdown_note: Literally 'fully rested out'. The positive counterpart to erschöpft. Ich bin ausgeruht = I am fully rested.

examples.de: Ich bin heute morgen ausgeruht und fit.
examples.en: I am rested and fit this morning.

examples.de: Nach dem Urlaub fühlt man sich ausgeruht.
examples.en: After the holiday one feels refreshed.

words.mnemonic: AUS-ge-RUHT: fully RESTED (ruhen) OUT (aus) — energised.

insight: die Sucht (addiction) and süchtig (addicted) come from the verb suchen (to seek/search) — originally meant a sickness or craving that drives you to keep searching. ⚠ die Abhängigkeit (dependence/addiction) vs. die Unabhängigkeit (independence) — perfect antonyms: ab-hängig = hanging off something (dependent); un-abhängig = not hanging off anything. der Entzug = withdrawal — literally 'the pulling away' (entziehen = to withdraw/deprive). Used in: Drogenentzug (drug withdrawal), Alkoholentzug (alcohol withdrawal).

breakdown.note: from suchen = to seek — originally meant compulsive searching/sickness

words.breakdown_note: Originally meant a compulsive sickness/craving — someone who kept 'seeking' something they couldn't stop. Related to suchen (to seek).

examples.en: Alcohol addiction is a serious illness.
He is fighting his addiction.

word_family.meaning: to seek — ⚠ historical root, not modern meaning

words.mnemonic: SUCHT: from SUCHEN (to seek) — you keep compulsively seeking more.

examples.en: He is addicted to nicotine.
Social media is addictive.

words.grammar_notes: süchtig nach + Dative = addicted to: Er ist süchtig nach Koffein.
words.mnemonic: SÜCHTIG: Sucht + -ig = 'having the quality of addiction'.

words.breakdown_note: Literally 'hanging off something' — dependent on it. Antonym: die Unabhängigkeit (independence) — not hanging off anything.

examples.de: Die Abhängigkeit von Medikamenten ist problematisch.
examples.en: Dependence on medication is problematic.

examples.de: Er hat eine körperliche Abhängigkeit entwickelt.
examples.en: He has developed a physical dependency.

words.mnemonic: AB-HÄNGIG-KEIT: HANGING (hängen) OFF (ab) something — dependent on it.

examples.de: Er ist stark von Koffein abhängig.
examples.en: He is heavily dependent on caffeine.

examples.de: Die Entscheidung ist von vielen Faktoren abhängig.
examples.en: The decision depends on many factors.

words.grammar_notes: abhängig von + Dative: Er ist abhängig von Alkohol. Also used generally: Das hängt von dir ab (That depends on you).
words.mnemonic: AB-HÄNGIG: hanging OFF something — you're hooked.

words.breakdown_note: Literally 'the pulling away/removing'. Einen Entzug machen = to go through withdrawal. Der Alkoholentzug = alcohol withdrawal. Also used generally: Nahrungsentzug = food deprivation.

examples.en: He is currently going through drug withdrawal.
The withdrawal symptoms were severe.

words.mnemonic: ENT-ZUG: pulling (Zug) away (ent-) the substance — withdrawal.

examples.de: Er hat zehn Jahre lang geraucht.
examples.en: He smoked for ten years.

examples.de: Rauchen ist in vielen öffentlichen Gebäuden verboten.
examples.en: Smoking is banned in many public buildings.

words.mnemonic: RAUCHEN: Rauch (smoke) + -en — to make smoke / to smoke.

words.english: to stop, to quit, to cease
words.breakdown_note: aufhören mit + Dative = to stop doing: aufhören mit dem Rauchen = to quit smoking. aufhören zu + Infinitive: Ich höre auf zu rauchen.

examples.de: Er hat mit dem Rauchen aufgehört.
examples.en: He has stopped smoking.
Stop it! Quit it!

word_family.meaning: to give up — near-synonym in quitting context

words.mnemonic: AUF-HÖREN: STOP listening to the craving — HEAR (hören) it no more.

insight: sich pflegen (to take care of oneself) vs. pflegen zu + Infinitive (to be in the habit of doing): Er pflegt nach dem Essen spazieren zu gehen (He is in the habit of going for a walk after eating). ⚠ die Reinigung (cleaning/purification) vs. die Reinheit (purity/cleanliness) — Reinigung is the process; Reinheit is the state. Also: die Reinigung = the dry cleaner's (shop). gepflegt as an adjective can describe both a person (well-groomed) and a place (well-kept) or even a conversation: ein gepflegtes Gespräch (a refined/civilised conversation).

examples.en: Personal care includes regular washing.

examples.de: Körperpflege ist ein wichtiger Teil des Alltags.
examples.en: Personal hygiene is an important part of daily life.

words.mnemonic: KÖRPER-PFLEGE: BODY (Körper) + CARE (Pflege) = personal care.

words.english: to take care of oneself, to groom oneself
words.breakdown_note: pflegen zu + Infinitive = to be in the habit of: Er pflegt nach dem Essen spazieren zu gehen (He is in the habit of walking after dinner). This is a distinct formal use.

examples.en: She takes great care of herself.

examples.de: Er pflegt zu sagen, dass Gesundheit das Wichtigste ist.
examples.en: He is in the habit of saying that health is the most important thing.

words.mnemonic: SICH PFLEGEN: take CARE (pflegen) of yourself — self-care.

breakdown.note: from Greek Hygieia = goddess of health/cleanliness

examples.en: Good hygiene prevents diseases.

examples.de: Auf der Intensivstation ist Hygiene besonders wichtig.
examples.en: In intensive care hygiene is especially important.

words.mnemonic: HYGIENE: Greek goddess Hygieia — same word as in English.

words.breakdown_note: gepflegt can describe a person (well-groomed), a place (well-kept), or even a conversation/meal: ein gepflegtes Gespräch = a refined/civilised conversation; ein gepflegtes Bier = a well-poured beer.

examples.de: Er sieht immer sehr gepflegt aus.
examples.en: He always looks very well-groomed.
The garden was carefully kept.

words.mnemonic: GE-PFLEGT: past participle of pflegen as adj. — well-tended, well-cared-for.

words.breakdown_note: die Reinigung = (1) the act of cleaning/purification, (2) a dry cleaner's shop (Ich bringe mein Jackett zur Reinigung). Reinheit = the state of purity/cleanliness.

examples.de: Die Reinigung der Wunde ist wichtig.
examples.en: Cleaning the wound is important.

examples.de: Er brachte seinen Anzug zur Reinigung.
examples.en: He took his suit to the dry cleaner's.

words.mnemonic: REINIGUNG: rein (clean) + -ig- + -ung = 'the cleaning'.

words.breakdown_note: sauber = clean (the practical state). rein = pure/clean (more absolute, also moral purity). sauber machen = to clean/tidy. Sauberkeit = cleanliness.

examples.en: The room is clean.
Please clean the kitchen.

word_family.meaning: pure, clean — more absolute than sauber

words.mnemonic: SAUBER: 'ZOW-ber' — think of SCRUBBING until it's clean.

words.breakdown_note: Literally 'finding oneself well'. Used in formal contexts: körperliches und seelisches Wohlbefinden (physical and mental well-being).

examples.en: Sport promotes general well-being.

examples.de: Ihr Wohlbefinden liegt mir am Herzen.
examples.en: Your well-being is close to my heart.

word_family.meaning: how one is doing, state of health

words.mnemonic: WOHL-BE-FINDEN: finding (befinden) oneself WELL (wohl) — well-being.
